title: Affine-line support localization after the retraction
statement:
Fix the finite-field and finite-coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p_0$, $\ell\ne p_0$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, assume $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$, and set $N=n/e$. Use the affine-line datum [def-pur-affine-line-datum]: $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, projection $p:X\to Y$, zero section $s:Y\hookrightarrow X$, complementary open $j:U=\mathbf G_{m,Y}\hookrightarrow X$, and $\pi=pj$. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with derived direct images [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Put $F=A_X(1)[0]$, where the twist is the one in the affine-line datum. Let $Rs^!_0$ be the right derived functor on bounded-below complexes of $M\mapsto s^{-1}\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ [def-pur-flasque-support], and put $B_0=Rs^!_0F$, $P=Rp_*F$, $Q=R\pi_*A_U(1)[0]$.

The ring $A$ is finite; $Y,X,U$ are Noetherian, $X,U$ are finite type over $k$, and $j$ is quasi-compact. Here Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. The functor $s_*$ on these module sheaves is exact; its termwise derived functor is canonically $Rs_*$, commutes with shifts, and satisfies $\mathcal H^q(s_*L)=s_*\mathcal H^q(L)$ for every complex $L$ and integer $q$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The canonical composition comparisons of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] for $ps=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $pj=\pi$ identify the image under $Rp_*$ of the support localization triangle of [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle] with a distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$B_0\longrightarrow P\xrightarrow{r}Q\xrightarrow{\delta}B_0[1].$$
Its first arrow is the image of the support-adjunction counit $s_*B_0\to F$, and $r$ is the image of $F\to Rj_*j^*F$ under $Rp_*$ followed by the canonical composition comparison. These identifications are natural in the displayed input. No identification of $Rs^!_0$ with a transported exceptional functor is part of this assertion.

proof.text: By [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level], $A\cong(\mathbf Z/\ell^N\mathbf Z)^{ef}$ as a module, with $e,f,N$ finite positive integers. The right side has $(\ell^N)^{ef}$ elements, so $A$ is a finite commutative ring. The hypotheses $e\mid n$, $n\geq1$ and $\ell\ne p_0$ are precisely those of that lemma.

source.place: First paragraph, localization triangle through Rp_* and the identifications ps=id and pj=pi; returned steps 1-2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-affine-line-support-geometry] to the field $k$ and the finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$. Its $X,s,U,j$ are our affine-line pair. It gives finite type of $X,U$, Noetherianity of $Y,X,U$, and quasi-compactness of $j$.

source.place: First paragraph, localization triangle through Rp_* and the identifications ps=id and pj=pi; returned steps 1-2.

proof.text: By [lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact], $s_*$ is exact, since its complementary open $j$ is quasi-compact and $A$ is finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]: its termwise functor computes $Rs_*$ on every complex. Termwise application commutes with shifts by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. For a complex $L$, exactness preserves the kernel of $d^q$, the image of $d^{q-1}$ and their quotient, giving $\mathcal H^q(s_*L)=s_*\mathcal H^q(L)$, naturally; the same calculation shows that these identifications descend through quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; exactness preserves the kernels, images and quotients defining cohomology. Closed pushforward exactness is Tag 09BM, proetale.tex, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact.

proof.text: The degree-zero sheaf complex $F$ is bounded below. Apply [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle], using the finite ring and quasi-compact complement already checked. Its support functor is exactly $Rs^!_0$, so it gives $s_*B_0\xrightarrow{\epsilon}F\xrightarrow{\eta}Rj_*j^*F\xrightarrow{b}(s_*B_0)[1]$. In the model [def-pur-support-triangle] the first arrow is the supported-kernel inclusion and the second is the open unit. By [lem-sf-ringed-closed-kernel-adjoint], the kernel identification carries that inclusion to the sheaf support counit, and the derived counit is induced by this sheaf counit. Thus $\epsilon$ is the support-adjunction counit, with the triangle functoriality asserted by the localization theorem.

source.place: First paragraph, localization triangle through Rp_* and the identifications ps=id and pj=pi; returned steps 1-2.

proof.text: The module-sheaf categories admit K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], on the small sites stipulated in the statement. The functor $p_*$ is additive by [lem-weil-proetale-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Hence [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] applies to its ordinary right derived functor $Rp_*$ and makes the image of the preceding triangle distinguished, using its specified shift isomorphism $\sigma:Rp_*((s_*B_0)[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rp_*s_*B_0)[1]$.

source.place: First paragraph, localization triangle through Rp_* and the identifications ps=id and pj=pi; returned steps 1-2.

proof.text: In [def-pur-affine-line-datum], $ps=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $pj=\pi$; restriction of its twist gives $j^*F=A_U(1)[0]$, compatibly with base change by [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]. Since $\ell$ is invertible on these $k$-schemes, the finite-level, unrestricted comparison of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], together with $Rs_*=s_*$, gives natural isomorphisms $\alpha:Rp_*s_*B_0\xrightarrow{\sim}B_0$ and $\beta:Rp_*Rj_*j^*F\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$. They use the inverses of $c_{p,s}$ and $c_{p,j}$ and the canonical identity identification.

source.place: First paragraph, localization triangle through Rp_* and the identifications ps=id and pj=pi; returned steps 1-2.

proof.text: Transport the distinguished image triangle by $(\alpha,1_P,\beta)$ and its shifted first component. Explicitly its arrows are $u=Rp_*(\epsilon)\alpha^{-1}$, $r=\beta Rp_*(\eta)$, and $\delta=\alpha[1]\sigma Rp_*(b)\beta^{-1}$. The three squares commute by these formulas, so invariance under isomorphism of distinguished triangles gives $B_0\to P\to Q\to B_0[1]$. These formulas give the stated first two arrows. Every map and comparison used above is natural, so the same formulas commute with morphisms of the input. This proves the required naturality.

Step checks: (1) lem-pur-finite-kummer-level gives A≅(Z/ℓ^N)^{ef}, so A is finite; its hypotheses e|n, n≥1 and ℓ≠p0 match the item. (2) lem-pur-affine-line-support-geometry applies to the finite-type k-scheme Y and gives finite type of X and U, Noetherianity of Y, X and U, and quasi-compactness of j. (3) lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact (quasi-compact complement, finite ring) gives s_* exact; lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor says every complex computes Rs_*; lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated gives the shift compatibility; the H^q formula is an elementary kernel/image calculation and holds for unbounded L. Bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective, so the two derived functors agree on D^+. (5) K-injectives on small sites plus additivity of p_* make Rp_* triangulated by lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated, with σ as its shift comparison.
